subject: dplyr - error joining on yearmon dates

messages.author: fb6cce9b1350698d
messages.subject: dplyr - error joining on yearmon dates
parts:
I get the following when I try and do a join on dates with the class of yearmon:

Joining by: "dates"
Error: cannot join on columns 'dates' x 'dates': Can't join on 'dates' x 'dates' because of incompatible types (yearmon / yearmon) 

Is this expected? I wouldn't be surprised if I'm doing it wrong. However, looking at various issues and discussion leading up to #1105 I think this should work.

I'm using the latest lazyeval and dplyr from github.

--pete


Example:

library(dplyr)
library(zoo)

foo <- structure(list(dates = structure(c(2L, 1L, 3L), 
                                        .Label = c("Feb 2015", 
                                                   "Jan 2015", 
                                                   "Mar 2015"), 
                                        class = "factor"), 
                      var1 = c(1, 2, 3)), 
                 .Names = c("dates", "var1"), 
                 row.names = c(NA, -3L), 
                 class = "data.frame")

bar <- structure(list(dates = structure(c(2L, 1L, 3L), 
                                        .Label = c("Feb 2015", 
                                                   "Jan 2015", 
                                                   "Mar 2015"), 
                                        class = "factor"), 
                      var2 = c(10, 20, 30)), 
                 .Names = c("dates", "var2"), 
                 row.names = c(NA, -3L), 
                 class = "data.frame")

baz <- full_join(foo, bar) # ok

foo$dates <- as.yearmon(foo$dates)
bar$dates <- as.yearmon(bar$dates)

qux <- full_join(foo, bar) # nope

> "Jan 2015",
> "Mar 2015"),
> class = "factor"),
> var1 = c(1, 2, 3)),

Thanks David.

Sorry, I should have been clearer in my question.

I know how to avoid the problem, I was just wondering if I was trying to do something not supported. I do a lot of work with dates in yearmon, converting back and forth to character just gives me more places to make an error.

Looking at the problems closed with the one referenced above (in particular #1028), it seemed to me that the zoo classes should be working.

--pete
